subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
passage:
Jomon, put that phone down a moment. I'm Raghav, and I want to tell you about a night when I was twenty. A message reached our hostel group: a photo of a tea-stall owner supposedly beating a child, and the words “Share until he's shamed.” Thirty of us boys were furious. Somebody said, “Let's go to the stall now.”

My thumb was over the share button. Something made me pause. I asked, “Where was this taken?” Nobody knew. I rang Suresh, whose family lives near that stall. “The stall is closed for a wedding,” he said. “The old man is at home.”

The photo turned out to be from another town, years old. Afterwards I thought about the tea-stall owner, Manohar, who never knew how close a crowd had come. I still wait ten minutes before I share anything.

qa.q: What did Raghav ask when the message arrived?
Why did Raghav pause with a thumb over the share button?
qa.a: Despite the group's fury, Raghav felt uneasy and doubtful, and wanted to know the source first, since a photo without a place or date proved nothing.

qa.q: What did Raghav do to check the message before sharing?
qa.a: Raghav rang Suresh, whose family lives near the stall, and learned the stall was closed and the owner was at home.

qa.q: What might have happened to Manohar if the crowd had gone to the stall that night?
qa.a: Manohar, an innocent old man, could have been frightened or hurt by an angry crowd over a false photo, without ever knowing why.

grounding: A young adult checks the source of a viral accusation before sharing, and the pause breaks the chain that turns anger into a mob.

passage:
Sangeeta's bus was three stops from home, and her phone said 5%. A video was flooding the residents' group: a delivery man supposedly stealing from a parcel locker, angry messages piling up beneath it. Yogesh had already typed, “Report him to the police right now!”

Her thumb hovered over the share button. She felt her own anger rising. Then she took one slow breath and tapped the username on the video. It was a new account. She searched the caption, and the same clip appeared from another city, months old, with a different story.

“Yogesh, wait,” she typed. “This video is old and from somewhere else. Let's check before we name anyone.”

The phone died before he replied. At her stop she saw that the group had gone quiet.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta's phone say when the bus was three stops from home?
What was Sangeeta feeling when the thumb hovered over the share button?
qa.a: Sangeeta felt anger rising, yet paused to breathe before acting.

qa.q: What steps did Sangeeta take before sharing the video?
qa.a: Sangeeta tapped the username, saw a new account, searched the caption and found the same clip from another city, months old.

qa.q: How might the delivery man have been affected if the video had kept spreading?
qa.a: The delivery man could have been wrongly named and shamed, or even threatened, for something never done.

grounding: A young adult under time pressure checks the source of a viral accusation before sharing, breaking the chain that turns anger into a mob.
